description: Configure response, failure or delay rules for supported requests intercepted by the app integration. Coverage depends on transport, hooks and rule-loading timing; early startup requests may bypass a rule. Inspect existing rules before editing, trigger the intended request and check observed results. Simulated offline behavior does not disconnect the device. Remove rules created for this task afterward or restore prior settings; preserve unrelated rules. Requires Buoy Pro and network override support.

action.description: add creates a rule (or replaces one when `id` is given). remove drops one by `id`. clear drops all. enable/disable flip ONE rule when `id` is given, otherwise the master switch — rules are kept either way. list shows every rule with its hit counts; pass `id` to dump one rule in full, body included. debug reports why a rule is or isn't firing.

alternate.description: Apply to every OTHER matching request, forever: the first goes through, the second is overridden, and so on. This is how you test retry logic and flaky endpoints — a rule that is always on or always off can't reach those paths.

body.description: For kind 'respond': the response body. Pass JSON directly (an object or array) or a raw string; content-type is inferred.

bodyPatch.description: For `add` with `fromRequestId` (or a rule `id`): fields deep-merged INTO the real captured response — the way to change one field of a big payload without pasting it back. Send only what changes, e.g. {"name":"test123"}. Ignored when `body` is given.

delayMs.description: Latency before the outcome, in ms. Works with every kind.

deviceId.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices or from your instructions. Pass it whenever more than one app may be connected. Once a call names a device, later calls in this session use it when deviceId is left out.

enabled.description: For `add`: whether the rule is enabled. Default true; pass false to stage it switched off. Useful for staging a rule you'll arm later with enable({id}).

fromRequestId.description: For `add`: build the rule from a captured request id (from get_network_requests) — the same 'Override this request' the developer gets in the UI. Seeds the pattern (query string replaced with `*` so it keeps matching), the method, the status, and the REAL response body, so you can change two fields of a payload you just saw instead of authoring one from scratch. Anything you pass explicitly overrides the prefill.

headers.description: For kind 'respond': response headers to send.

id.description: Rule id. Required for `remove`. For `add` it replaces that rule. For `enable`/`disable` it targets ONE rule instead of the master switch. For `list` it dumps that rule in full.

kind.description: respond = return your status/body, never hitting the network (default). fail = a transport failure, as if the device were offline. delay = let the real request run, just late.

methods.description: For `add`: restrict to these HTTP methods. Omit for any.

name.description: Label shown in the developer's UI.

status.description: For kind 'respond': HTTP status, 200–599 (default 200). Outside that range fetch itself throws, so use kind 'fail' for connection errors rather than status 0.

statusText.description: For kind 'respond': the status line's text, e.g. 'Service Unavailable'. Cosmetic — React Native's XMLHttpRequest has no statusText field, so the app never sees it; it only makes the developer's rule list read correctly.

times.description: Auto-disable the rule after N matches. Use 1 for 'make the next call fail' so it can't linger.

url.description: For `debug`: a concrete URL to test the rules against, so the report says which rule would match it and why.

urlPattern.description: For `add`: glob matched against the WHOLE request URL, query string included. `*` is the only wildcard, e.g. '*pokeapi.co*' or 'https://api.example.com/v1/users*'. Careful with an exact URL copied from get_network_requests — if the client cache-busts or pages, the next call won't match it and the rule sits at 0 hits. Prefer `fromRequestId`, which handles that for you.

name: network_override
